formula_checks.name: periodTotalReturn
formula_checks.auditor_why: Claims same total as periodReturn, but periodReturnParts refuses short history instead of returning the first-price fallback.
formula_checks.why: The "refuses short history" claim is false in code: closeAsOf falls back to the first close (DEC-4641), so periodTotalReturn and periodReturn both give +9.93% in the five-month example. The card's words for MK-PF-F-039 leave that fallback out: the master file's card needs it added (file and code must match).

formula_checks.name: periodReturnParts
formula_checks.auditor_why: Start reader has no first-price fallback although DEC-4641 and periodReturn require it; its branch computing short-history years is then unreachable.
formula_checks.why: Same fallback, so the two-year short-history branch is reached: 14 months up 21% reads +17.80% a year (fact test). Card text needs the fallback.

formula_checks.name: returnSincePurchases
formula_checks.auditor_why: On a later purchase day it measures old shares at that evening close before adding the new purchase; this is an end-of-day cash-flow convention. Undated purchases get invented dates.
formula_checks.why: Both claims hold: a later purchase is placed at the end of its day, against DEC-4439 (+26.76% where +15.24% is right), and an undated purchase is put on a guessed day (tenet 3).

formula_checks.name: isoDay
formula_checks.auditor_why: Correct on the stated finite, valid-input domain. This is a specification judgment; ingestion, actual UI and app execution are not provided.
formula_checks.why: Five of five cases agree, both time-zone crossings included.

formula_checks.name: windowTotal
formula_checks.auditor_why: Missing years defaults to 0 and can turn a yearly rate into a window total by assertion.
formula_checks.why: Years defaulting to 0 never turns a yearly rate into a total in the app: every row carries its total and the one caller reading yearly rates (gainOfRow) passes the years. Making periodTotal required on the row type would close the door; no figure is wrong today.

formula_checks.name: windowTotalOfRow
formula_checks.auditor_why: It passes no years, so a legacy 2Y row at 10%/year without periodTotal returns 10% as the two-year total rather than 21%.
formula_checks.why: No row without a window total exists (fact test: 16 of 16 rows carry it), so the 2Y "legacy row" cannot reach it.

formula_checks.name: startValues
formula_checks.auditor_why: Present value / growth factor gives synthetic starts when quantities change; zero-valued total-loss positions are omitted, biasing the result upward.
formula_checks.why: Working the start back from the return is DEC-5068's approved formula; it misstates the start when shares were bought inside the window (needs his ruling). Leaving out a holding that lost everything is wrong by tenet 4 (case level).

FIX-1.example: 10 shares at $100 on Sep 1 (close $100), 10 more at $110 on Sep 2 (close $121), today $121.
FIX-1.moves: The window figure of a holding first bought inside the window and bought again on a later day: Performance holding rows, account page holding rows, Holding page; and what adds those rows up where the beginning is worked back (wealth generated and Return, MK-PF-M-002 / MK-PF-M-016), and each category's return (MK-PF-M-006).
FIX-1.drawings: Holding detail v02's holding was first bought in 2023 (before its window), so it does not move. A text search of Performance v17 and account page v01 found no holding first bought inside its window; confirm against the figures when the fix is made.

RULING-1.ids: MK-PF-F-044 startValues → MK-PF-M-008 Home "market +X%" (the same formula sits in MK-NW-F-138 knownHoldingsReturn, DEC-5068)
RULING-1.question_in_plain_words: When shares were bought during the window, how much was the holding worth when the window began?
RULING-1.example: A: 10 shares at $100 when the window opens, 10 more bought at $110 mid-window, now 20 × $121 = $2,420 (its yardstick +10%). B: $1,000, flat (its yardstick +2%).
RULING-1.today: market +7.33% (A counted as worth $2,000 at the start: $2,420 ÷ 1.21)
RULING-1.other_reading: market +6.00% (A counted as the $1,000 it was really worth)
RULING-1.recommended: +6.00%: the figure's own definition says "weighted by what that holding was worth when the window began", and $1,000 is what it was worth.

RULING-2.ids: MK-ST-F-081 timeWeightedReturn → MK-PF-M-016 / MK-PF-M-017 Return, Home "you +X%"
RULING-2.question_in_plain_words: What does the return say when an account ends a day worth less than nothing (it owes more than it holds, e.g. a margin debt)?
RULING-2.where_on_screen: Performance Return, the account page Return, Home "you +X%".
RULING-2.today: −100.00% (the value is floored at $0) — rules out by tenet 7: it looks better than it is
RULING-2.other_reading: −108.32% (the true change), or no figure with a sentence saying the account owes more than it holds
RULING-2.recommended: No figure, with that sentence: the next day would have nothing to grow from, which the app already refuses (DEC-0316).
